subject: Reserved fleet expansion & staged traffic-shift schedule
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Joe Thomas <joe@saasco.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.procurement@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal + capacity add-on (reserved fleet)

Hi Joe —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our discussion I'm attaching an updated renewal proposal (v3) that adds 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs across two pools:
- pool-alpha (latency-optimized): 24 GPUs, burst buffer for low-latency traffic
- pool-beta (batch/throughput): 16 GPUs, higher batch sizes for embeddings/rerank

Key commercial changes included in v3: 12-month term, 10% list discount off Dedicated rates, and a committed throughput SLA (p95 token latency target and 99.5% availability for dedicated pools).

You asked for an operational plan that minimizes risk during the cutover — below is a short ask so we can produce a staged runbook:
1) Confirm preferred 4-hour maintenance window (US-Pacific preferred)
2) Approve canary traffic slice (suggest 5% traffic to new pool for 24 hours)
3) Confirm whether SaaSCo will run any heavy regen tasks during cutover (we recommend pausing large training/eval jobs)

I've attached the proposal PDF. If that looks good I'll follow up with a technical staging plan and a traffic-shift schedule that your engineering team can sign off on.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: SaaSCo_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity add-on (reserved fleet)

Marcus —

Thanks for the update and proposal. High level this looks good. A few quick points from our side:
- Procurement will need an itemized cost sheet with per-pool unit economics (can you surface expected tokens/sec and $/1000 tokens for the two pools?)
- Engineering wants a low-risk cutover plan. The 5% canary sounds reasonable but we need an explicit rollback plan and a health probe definition.
- Our preferred maintenance windows are Tue/Wed 00:00–04:00 PT.

Alice (cc) will drive legal/procurement. Marcus — please share the staging plan and checklist so we can loop in our infra/ops leads.

—Joe
Director of Product, SaaSCo
joe@saasco.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Joe Thomas <joe@saasco.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.procurement@saasco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity add-on (reserved fleet)

Joe —

Appreciate the quick notes. Attached is a short staging-plan.xlsx and a traffic-shift checklist (summary below). I've also included estimated unit economics per your ask; the spreadsheet has ranges based on expected sequence length distribution.

Staging & traffic-shift overview (summary):
- Pre-cutover (Week -1): provision pools + run internal smoke tests, share access to staging endpoint with SaaSCo engineers
- Canary (Day 0): shift 5% user requests to pool-alpha using weight-based routing for 24 hours; monitor latency p95, error-rate, and token throughput.
- Ramp (Day 1–3): increase to 20% / 50% / 80% over successive days if metrics stable
- Final cut (Day 4): schedule 1-hour freeze for DNS & routing change, shift remaining traffic to new pools, decommission temporary mapping after 48hr stable window

Rollback criteria (examples):
- p95 latency > agreed target by 30% for 10 min
- Error rate (5xx) increases > 0.5% over baseline for 5 min
- Model inference mismatch on verification prompts (automated check)

I'll have Laura and Grace coordinate the technical runbook and post cut checklist. If you confirm Tue/Wed 00:00–04:00 PT for the maintenance windows we can tentatively book the week of Sept 7th.

Attachments: staging-plan.xlsx, traffic-shift-checklist.md

Best,
Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 15:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + capacity add-on (reserved fleet) — internal runbook items

Team —

Quick internal checklist before we send the final runbook to SaaSCo:
1) Confirm pool sizing with infra (we need exact GPU types + NIC configs). Marcus — can you get the confirmed SKU list from provisioning?
2) Health probes: implement two probes — (a) latency p95 synthetic run using 10 curated prompts, (b) binary success probe for model checksum & kv-cache integrity. Rachel, please draft the probe specs and threshold alerts.
3) Telemetry hooks: ensure tracing headers are respected and include token-level metrics in the first 24 hours. Grace — add the tracing dashboards to the shared Drive folder.
4) Fallback policy: define automatic fallback to hosted variant if both pools fail; include cost implications in the notes.

I'll merge these into the staging-plan.xlsx and circulate. We should avoid heavy baseline jobs during the canary window — ping Joe to ask for a soft freeze for 48 hours starting Day -1.

Laura
Sr Delivery Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Staged shift schedule & signing request — SaaSCo renewal (RDW-2024-8471)

Hi Joe / Alice —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. Attached is the final staged-shift schedule (PDF exported from the spreadsheet) and the traffic-shift checklist. Summary of the agreed plan:
- Maintenance window: Tue 00:00–04:00 PT (primary), fallback Wed 00:00–04:00 PT
- Canary: 5% of production traffic to pool-alpha for 24h starting Tue 00:30 PT; automated health checks in place
- Ramp: 20% / 50% / 80% over subsequent 72h if no rollback triggers
- Final cut: Day 4, 1-hour freeze + decommission old mapping after 48h stable

Next steps for SaaSCo:
1) Alice — please review the line-item sheet (sheet 2 in the attachment) and confirm PO cadence.
2) Joe — can your infra leads confirm they can enforce the 48h soft freeze for large batch runs?
3) We need an e-signature to finalize commercial terms: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC123SaaSCo

If we get signature + PO by Sept 15, provisioning and pool warm-up will begin the week of Sept 21 and we can execute the cutover the week of Sept 28.

Regards,
